advisory.finding: When a ticket directory is removed, `_apply` deletes its `docs` row only by `dir_name`, but `_reindex` inserts the row under the reduced `ticket_id` (`doc[0]`), which it explicitly treats as potentially different from `dir_name`. If a ticket's reduced id differs from its directory name, the FTS `docs` row is inserted under the id but the drop-path deletes under the dir_name, orphaning the row in the index permanently.
scenarios: A ticket whose CREATE event `data.id` differs from its on-disk directory name is indexed (row keyed by data.id), then its directory is later removed — the drop deletes nothing and a stale document survives in search results forever.

ABSENCE: no test in test_similar_tickets_index.py or test_similar_tickets_scale.py runs catch_up twice after an index-producing run and asserts that the second run re-hashes but indexes 0 while the third run is fully warm (empty diff). test_catch_up_does_no_work_on_an_unchanged_store only runs catch_up once after _indexed(), so it never observes the post-index .cache.json write-back and convergence sequence the contract describes.
advisory.finding: The documented 'one run of lag then convergence' catch-up behavior is untested. catchup.py's docstring states that after any run that indexed something, re-indexing writes a .cache.json into the ticket directory AFTER live_entries read the mtime, so the NEXT catch-up re-hashes those exact directories (hash unchanged, nothing re-indexed) and the stored mtime converges, the run after that being fully warm. No test drives this sequence: a regression where catch-up re-indexes the same directories on every run (never converging / index thrash) would pass all existing tests, since test_catch_up_does_no_work_on_an_unchanged_store writes tickets via direct event files (no reducer .cache.json write-back) rather than exercising the reduce_ticket-produces-a-cache-write-back path the convergence contract describes.
